Shared inbox — three directions (design.md §6.1)

Same screen, same data, three deliberately different answers to "what should this feel like?". Pick one and I'll build the full screen set (board, work order detail, analytics, admin, phone simulator, mobile) in that direction.

A · Ops Console
For: front desk agents living in the inbox all shift.
Bet: density and speed — 6+ conversations visible, keyboard shortcuts on every action, mono room numbers, compact SLA chips.
Tradeoff: feels like software, not hospitality. Small targets on a phone.

B · Warm Hospitality
For: properties that want staff tools to feel like the brand.
Bet: warmth and calm — serif guest names, cream ground, plain-language copy ("Guests waiting", "Texts OK"), roomier rows.
Tradeoff: ~30% fewer conversations per screen; less at-a-glance status.

C · Night Shift
For: back-of-house and shift boards; also the strongest base for department staff on phones.
Bet: high contrast, big 44px targets, countdown timers as the primary signal, dark for dim environments.
Tradeoff: dark UI in a bright lobby on a shared front-desk screen; loud.
